On it. Quick note on what went wrong and my workaround: the original invite was forwarded by one of your coordinators (Alex) rather than being a calendar update from our org. When that happens GCal sometimes keeps the event but strips the internal meet/join anchor — and Exchange will reject invites where the organizer address doesn't match expected domain policies.

Workaround steps I followed:
1) Created a brand new event from kimberly@redwood.com (Organizer: Kimberly Park)
2) Added Google Meet (meet.google.com/rnd-xxxx-xxxx) as the primary join URL in the event details
3) Added FinTrain attendees (alex.rivera@fintrain.com, liam.oconnor@fintrain.com, priya.singh@fintrain.com) and Redwood attendees (priym@redwood.com, ben@redwood.com)
4) Set visibility to default and sent the invites (not a forward).

I hit an odd warning when publishing — GCal logged a "organizer mismatch" because the forwarded event id still existed on the recipient side. I exported the publish log and attached the relevant lines in case your IT wants to trace it.

Attachment: gcal-fwd-log.txt (text/plain)

I published the new event for May 9 at 1:00pm PT as you suggested — seat check: 30 minutes. Alex, you should see a fresh invite from Kimberly Park / Redwood Inference with a Meet link. If Priya still cannot accept, I can create the event from a different Redwood account or add her manually as a guest.

-Kim
